title: Orchard Health - Contract + KMS Onboarding Sync
summary: Initial procurement intake and security handoff for Redwood Dedicated/Private options. Customer requires KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, DPA redlines, SLA clarifications and a pricing path including a 3-month pilot. SE to run benchmark on their 4k token p50 workload. Legal to review MSA/DPA redlines; procurement to align on billing and PO terms.
topics: Data residency and private VPC deployment
Pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity + pilot
Audit logs, retention, and SOC2 evidence
action_items: Maya Patel: Send annotated MSA+DPA with our standard redlines highlighted by 2026-10-14
Liam Chen: Schedule and run perf benchmark (4k token p50, 5k reqs/day) and share results by 2026-10-18
Isabel Gomez: Share security pack and SOC2/ISO artifacts link by 2026-10-13
Sarah Park: Share PO template and billing contact by 2026-10-15
next_steps: Redwood to share MSA/DPA redlines and security pack
SE to run benchmark on Dedicated vs Private for Orchard's workload
Pricing proposal for 3-month pilot and 12-month reserved option

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Isabel (Redwood CSM), Sarah (Orchard Head Procurement), Raj (Orchard InfoSec), Elena (CTO), Jared (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated summary: Procurement intake + security hand-off for Dedicated/Private deployment; MSA/DPA redlines and KMS requirements discussed.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:07] Sarah: hi this is sarah park from orchard procurement, we got elena, raj and jared on too.
[00:12] Elena: yeah thanks, morning all.
[00:14] Raj: raj mehta, info sec.
[00:17] Liam: liam chen, se at redwood, i'll take the technical bits.
[00:20] Isabel: isabel from cs, will help with onboarding timeline.
[00:24] Maya: cool, objective today — align on msadpa redlines, kms/hsm options for key management, sla expectations, and next steps for pricing and pilot.

[02:03] Sarah: i'll start with procurement constraints — our standard is net 45 PO terms, we'd like a sample ssa or po path. also we have a couple standard dpa exceptions: limited liability caps for pseudonymized data, and we ask for a data residency clause — production data must remain in our us-east region.

[03:12] Maya: okay that's helpful. on residency, redwood supports regional pinning for private deployments and we can pin models to us-east for Hosted as well but for strict residency private is the recommended path.

[04:05] Raj: big question is kms — we require customer-managed keys via our KMS (we use AWS KMS and a company HSM for certain workloads). can you support CMEK with HSM-backed keys and rotate keys on our cadence?

[04:38] Liam: short answer yes for private deployments. for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations and can support bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest; for hosted there are more constraints but we do offer envelope encryption. for HSM-backed we usually work with cloud HSM or managed HSM depending on the customer's cloud provider.

[05:22] Jared: curious about key usage in inference — are keys used per model or per tenant? any perf implications?

[05:35] Liam: keys are used for disk and blob encryption; the runtime doesn't decrypt token streams with the customer key in memory per request, instead we decrypt model artifacts at load time in a secure enclave and manage kv cache in encrypted memory. there's overhead at startup but steady-state QPS is negligible. will run the exact profile during the benchmark.

[07:01] Sarah: on the legal side, we have a DPA addendum that tightens data deletion timelines and requires 90-day retention for logs for audits. do you do audit logs at token level?

[07:25] Maya: we provide audit logs and detailed request/response traces at a metadata level, and you can opt into longer retention in the console — that's an add on. token-level scrubbing is available for PII redaction pipelines but we'll need to align on exact retention and redaction rules in the DPA.

[08:30] Raj: also need to confirm SOC2 scope and any ISO stuff. do you have SOC2 type 2?

[08:40] Isabel: yes we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 artifacts; i'll share the security pack and contact to our compliance team after the call.

[09:15] Elena: main product question — latency p50/p95 for our 4k token use case. we saw numbers on your site but want real-world benchmarks against our payloads.

[09:30] Liam: totally, we'll run dedicated and private variants. for a 4k token generation p50 on our ded. config we've seen ~220ms per chunk but that depends on model and quantization. we'll benchmark with your prompt set; can you share sample prompts and expected concurrency?

[10:05] Jared: expecting about 5k requests/day, peaks of ~250 concurrent during batch jobs, typical interactive concurrency closer to 30.

[10:30] Liam: that helps — we'll simulate mixed load with KV caching turned on and with/without prefix caching. aim to replicate p50/p95 and throughput.

[12:00] Sarah: pricing — procurement needs a clear pricing path. we want cost predictability. interested in a 3-month pilot on dedicated reserved capacity then move to an annual commit. how do you price piloting vs reserved?

[12:25] Maya: standard approach: pilot priced at a short-term reserved rate with a small uplift to account for churn; if you convert to 12-month commit we credit pilot fees toward annual. we'll send a pricing illustration. also note there are add-ons for extended log retention and private deployment setup fees.

[13:10] Raj: liability cap and indemnification language — in our msadpa we usually ask for a higher cap for security incidents and vendor to carry cyber E&O. what do you typically accept?

[13:30] Maya: our standard MSA has a liability cap that's often 12 months of fees; for enterprise we can discuss higher caps and standalone cyber policies. our legal is open to negotiating on a per-deal basis.

[14:02] Elena: question about backup and disaster recovery for private deploy — RTO/RPO targets?

[14:15] Liam: for private/on-prem deployments we offer backup snapshots and can commit to RTO windows depending on architecture — typical RTO for our private customers is 4 hours with daily snapshots; for Dedicated (hosted) we have cross-region failover patterns and SLA-backed uptime. we'll document specifics in the SRE runbook we share.

[15:40] Sarah: can you confirm breach notification timing? ours requires 72 hours for regulated data incidents.

[15:50] Maya: we commit to notification in line with regulatory windows; our default is 72 hours for incidents affecting customer data, but we'll confirm with legal.

[17:10] Jared: technical deep-dive follow-up — we may need to validate KV cache behavior with our RLHF-style prompts where context windows are long. is there a known degradation?

[17:30] Liam: KV cache lessens costs and latency for repeated prefixes but with long-context RLHF it depends on policy; we'll include RLHF-like workloads in the benchmark. we also can test different quantization levels; that influences perf and quality tradeoffs.

[19:05] Sarah: procurement path — once we get redlines we route to our legal counsel and should have a decision window in ~2 weeks. prerequisite is PO and pricing clarity.

[19:30] Maya: understood. we'll prioritize the MSA/DPA redline email and the pricing worksheet so you can route internally.

[21:00] Elena: question on audit logs — you mentioned longer retention is an add-on. can we get a retention SLA and chain of custody for logs?

[21:20] Isabel: yes we'll include retention SLAs and the chain of custody descriptions in the security pack. there are export options to your SIEM or S3 bucket as well.

[22:45] Raj: encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.3 and mutual TLS for private endpoints?

[22:55] Liam: yes TLS 1.3 supported; mutual TLS available for private endpoints and dedicated VPC peering. we'll document cert rotation processes.

[24:30] Sarah: are there any compliance templates for healthcare data handling? even though Orchard isn't a covered entity, some of our partners are healthcare providers.

[24:45] Isabel: we have a healthcare compliance note and BAAs are available for specific use cases; i'll flag with legal to assess need.

[26:00] Maya: circling back to pricing — can you confirm expected monthly token volume estimate so we can craft an accurate proposal?

[26:12] Jared: estimate is ~120M tokens/month, spikes to 200M in seasonal windows.

[26:30] Liam: ok that's helpful. that level usually benefits from reserved pricing and quantized models to save on unit cost. we'll run cost models in the pricing worksheet.

[28:00] Sarah: procurement will need a standard invoice sample and the PO flow. do you accept net 30 for pilots?

[28:12] Maya: pilots usually net 30 if there's an enterprise sales agreement; procurement's net 45 request may be an issue but we can accommodate net 45 on the annual contract. will escalate the payment terms to finance for pilot acceptance.

[30:00] Elena: on the private option — how long to onboard private deployment on prem? what's the delivery timeline?

[30:20] Liam: end-to-end private deployment for on-prem average timeline is 8–12 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM procurement; for VPC-hosted private it's typically 4–6 weeks. we'll propose a project plan.

[32:10] Raj: do you run penetration tests and can we request a third-party pentest report?

[32:20] Isabel: yes we run internal and external pentests annually and can share summaries; third-party reports can be provided under NDA.

[33:50] Sarah: ok high level recap?
[33:55] Maya: sure — action list: we'll send MSA+DPA redlines, security pack (SOC2/ISO), pricing worksheet with pilot vs 12-month reserved, and SE will run a load/latency benchmark with your prompts. legal sync next week to discuss DPA exceptions.

[34:20] Sarah: sounds good. also include a sample PO and invoice flow.

[34:30] Maya: noted. any blockers from your side?

[34:35] Elena: none immediate; need internal counsel review but timeline's fine.

[36:00] Raj: one more — are there data deletion guarantees for caches and backups? want timeline and proof of deletion on contract.

[36:12] Liam: deletion flows can be documented; for private we can commit to specific deletion windows and provide certificate of deletion for backups if required. we'll include that language for review.

[38:00] Sarah: procurement will expect an SLA with uptime and credits. do you map p50/p95 to credits?

[38:12] Maya: yes we have uptime SLAs and credits for breaches. performance SLOs like p95 are usually covered in technical runbooks and we can offer performance credits in enterprise contracts— we'll propose language.

[40:00] Isabel: i'll attach the SOC2 report link and a checklist for onboarding tasks after the call.

[41:05] Jared: small question: does redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?

[41:15] Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning both supported; we'll include admin setup steps.

[43:00] Sarah: ok how soon can we expect the redlines and pricing?

[43:10] Maya: we'll aim to send redlines and security pack by 2026-10-14 and pricing + benchmark plan by 2026-10-15.

[44:20] Raj: are there penalties for data residency breaches? will need to discuss with counsel.

[44:30] Maya: we'll surface recommended language and negotiating levers but counsel conversation needed.

[46:00] Elena: if pilot goes well, what's the fastest path to production?

[46:10] Liam: typically pilot->validation (2–4 weeks) -> procurement/legal finalize -> onboarding -> production cutover. overall 6–10 weeks after pilot conversion.

[47:30] Sarah: do you have references from other healthcare-adjacent customers?

[47:40] Maya: yes we can share reference contacts under NDA; i'll coordinate offline.

[49:00] Raj: any competitive differentiators we should be aware of?

[49:10] Liam: production-first runtime optimizations, dedicated caching strategies, and explicit guidance for cost/perf tradeoffs; plus a unified dev experience across hosted and private deployments.

[50:30] Sarah: ok let's lock on dates for the legal sync — can we do next tuesday?

[50:40] Maya: next tuesday 11/10? actually next tuesday would be 2026-10-20. is that good?

[50:50] Sarah: yes 2026-10-20 works for us.

[51:00] Maya: great i'll send calendar invite.

[52:10] Elena: thanks everyone — appreciate the clarity.

[52:20] Maya: quick recap — deliverables and owners repeated, and we will follow up with calendar and links.

[53:00] Sarah: thanks, talk soon.
[53:05] Raj: thanks.
[53:07] Jared: thanks all.

[53:15] Meeting end

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker attribution errors possible; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., HSM/H M S, KV cache spelled 'k v cache'). Links referenced: security pack (link to be sent), pricing worksheet (link to be sent), MSA/DPA redlines (attachment to email).
